back: Weathering and mass movement acting on the land above the reach of the waves, such as freeze–thaw, salt crystal growth, rockfall and slumping.
Waves undercut the base to form a notch; the unsupported rock collapses; waves remove the debris; the cycle repeats.
A gently sloping rock surface (about 1–3°) at the foot of a cliff, formed by cliff retreat, abrasion and weathering; it reduces wave energy.

front: Order of landforms on a headland
back: Cave, arch, stack, stump. A geo is a separate feature formed when the roof of a cave or blowhole collapses.
A coast where the bands of rock lie parallel to the shore; example Dalmatian coast of Croatia and Lulworth Cove.
A coast where the rock bands lie at right angles to the shore, giving alternating headlands and bays; example Swanage Bay and the Purbeck headlands.
Rockfall from steep jointed cliffs, landslides and rotational slumping in saturated clay, and mudflows of saturated soil.
Freeze–thaw (below 0 °C), salt crystal growth, carbonation and solution of limestone, and hydrolysis of feldspar.
Rate (m per year) = distance retreated ÷ time; volume lost = length × height × retreat; mass = volume × density.
